name.description: Binding name, 1 to 63 characters of letters, digits, '-', '_' and '.', starting with a letter or digit. It is what request records carry.

match.description: The source the binding applies to. Exactly one of cidr, ingress_if, vlan, vni and ipsec_tunnel. All but cidr match on the interface the connection arrived on.

cidr.description: IPv4 networks in a.b.c.d/len form, without host bits, that the socket peer of the request is in. At most 256.

ingress_if.description: Name of the interface the connection arrived on, at most 15 characters: the logical device, which for a tagged VLAN is its bridge (vlan<id>), for a VXLAN its device (vxlan<vni>) and for an IPsec tunnel its VTI. The name is stored, never an index, so an interface that is removed and created again keeps its binding. A name that does not exist on the node is accepted with a warning in the reply and matches nothing until it exists; an interface that is removed later is logged and matches nothing until it is back. The interface is that of the connection's first packet and holds for the life of the connection.

vlan.description: A VLAN ID. Another spelling of ingress_if: the VLAN's bridge interface on this node, vlan<id>.

vni.description: A VXLAN network identifier. Another spelling of ingress_if: the interface vxlan<vni> on this node.

ipsec_tunnel.description: Name of an IPsec tunnel configured on this node (/config/ipsec/tunnel). Another spelling of ingress_if: the tunnel's VTI interface, vti<mark>. A tunnel that is not configured, or has no mark, is accepted with a warning and matches nothing until it has one.

services.description: The AI services the binding applies to, each as VIP:port (IPv4). Empty or omitted applies it to every AI service. A service does not have to exist yet. At most 256.

tenant.description: The tenant a matching request is attributed to, 1 to 127 bytes. The same namespace as API-key and JWT tenants: its limits are the ones configured for that tenant.

allowed_models.description: The models a request admitted or held by this binding may name, compared exactly. Empty or omitted allows any. At most 256.

enforce.description: advisory (default): a request that presents a credential is decided by it and the binding is only noted. strict: a credential whose tenant is not the binding's is refused with 403 network_tenant_mismatch, and the model must also pass allowed_models. In both, a request with no credential on a service that does not require one is admitted as the binding's tenant.

credential.description: none (default): the binding never stands in for a credential. network: on a service that requires a credential, a request that presents none is admitted as the binding's tenant. Accepted with an interface match only (ingress_if, vlan, vni or ipsec_tunnel); refused with a cidr match. Also refused when a named service has a rule that is not an AI-gateway service and runs sockMapMode request or both: the gateway does not see every request on it.

forward_identity.description: Forward the request's tenant upstream as X-Auth-Tenant, and its user as X-Auth-User when it has one, on a request whose source matched this binding. Needs a non-empty services list, and is refused without one. The services the binding names then also drop every header whose name starts with X-Auth- that a client sends, on every request and whatever the rule's api_key_auth, whether or not the request's source matched a binding. A service no such binding applies to is unchanged. The identity is injected only on an AI-gateway service, where the admission gate decides it, and not into a chunked HTTP/1.1 request. Refused when a service the binding names has a rule that is not an AI-gateway service and runs sockMapMode request or both: the gateway does not see every request on it. Such a rule is refused in turn while the binding exists. Default false.

priority_class.description: The highest priority class a request the binding names the tenant of may have. It can only lower what the tenant allows (a tenant that sets no class allows standard). Default standard - a binding that should not cap its requests says critical.

fail_mode.description: What the binding's services do with a request while the binding lookup itself cannot answer (an internal fault, counted in loxilb_ai_netid_resolver_faults_total). neutral (default): the request is decided as if the service had no binding - it is never admitted by its network, and a valid credential is not refused, so a strict binding is not enforced during the fault. closed: every request the lookup would have decided is refused with 503 netid_unavailable until it answers again. The setting is per service in effect, not per binding: a service fails closed when any binding that applies to it says closed, whether that binding names the service or names none, and then it does so for every source. When the bindings that apply to a service disagree, the reply to the POST is "Success; warning: fail_mode: ..." and names them.
